title: Cloud runs' status model reads their records under the factory run id, but the container writes them under epic-<epic-id>
description:
cloudStatusModel/statusRecords open the run-state store with RunID = the factory's run_<hex>, yet a cloud run's orchestrator container runs ticfac run-epic <epic>, whose records land on the integration branch under .ticfac/runs/epic-<epic-id>/. So a real cloud run's model reads empty records: attempts, findings, evidence, checkpoint and cost degrade to feed-and-graph only, the live frame never shows waves from records, and a hold on untriaged findings surfaces only through the feed's run_held line, never as the model's WaitFinding attention with its triage pointer. Local runs are unaffected (their runID is epic-<epic-id> by construction).

ticfac run epic-2jn created this tick by absorbing the finding f7b63de6cbe36d247a2a5d5727d2a424b7b19b82363a8aed415ff0aedefd2762 (reported by run-epic-2jn/tick-ejw/attempt-25): the finding was judged against the epic's definition of done and gates done item A5. The decision record — item id, verdict, observed or predicted, confidence — is .ticfac/runs/epic-2jn/absorptions/f7b63de6cbe36d247a2a5d5727d2a424b7b19b82363a8aed415ff0aedefd2762.json on the run branch.
notes:

The decision record is .ticfac/runs/epic-2jn/absorptions/f7b63de6cbe36d247a2a5d5727d2a424b7b19b82363a8aed415ff0aedefd2762.json on epic/2jn, and it says: no classifier prediction could be made — no classifier is configured for gating predictions — so the reporter's own claim decides: it breaks A5, and the finding is absorbed against that item. The claim is a prediction, scored later against what the done actually did
